preconditions.description: The number of people in the tree is between 1 and 100,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= ri <= n for ri in r) and len(r) == n
preconditions.description: Each person's parent is a valid person number or 0 (no parent), and the list of parents has exactly n entries.

preconditions.expression: not any(i == r[i-1] for i in range(1, n+1) if r[i-1] != 0)
preconditions.description: No person is their own parent (no direct self-loop).
The number of queries is between 1 and 100,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= vi <= n and 1 <= pi <= n for vi, pi in queries)
preconditions.description: Each query consists of a valid person number and a valid cousin degree.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly one answer for each query.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= answer <= n-1 for answer in output)
postconditions.description: Each answer is a non-negative integer representing the count of p-th cousins for the queried person.

postconditions.expression: all((vi, pi) in queries and answer == sum(1 for y in range(1, n+1) if y != vi and is_p_cousin(vi, y, pi, r)) for vi, pi, answer in zip(queries, output))
postconditions.description: For each query (vi, pi), the answer is the count of people y ≠ vi such that y is a pi-th cousin of vi, where is_p_cousin(vi, y, pi, r) is true if there exists a person z who is a pi-ancestor of both vi and y.
